detail.readme:
# Swarm Rebuild A Chrome extension that wipes any web page to a blank canvas and lets a swarm of multiplayer cursors build it back, live: crosshair-drawn boxes, typed text, pen-tool lines, ruler guides and ⌥-drag duplicates, until the page looks just like it did before. ![Swarm Rebuild rebuilding a page](media/demo.webp) **[Install from the Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/swarm-rebuild/diaeaocnhdhbknkbfbnkjikfcgokainm)** · [Full demo video (36s)](media/demo.mp4) · [Demo with sound (60s)](media/demo-with-sound.mp4) ## Credit This is a tribute to **[Swarm](https://califa.github.io/swarm-site/)** by **[Joel Califa](https://joelcalifa.com)** ([@califa](https://github.com/califa), [source](https://github.com/califa/swarm-site)), a website that builds itself as you scroll. The motion design is his: the cursor set, the swarm and flocking physics, the build choreography (rects, typing, guides, duplicates), the rulers and the overall look. Large parts of the animation engine here are adapted directly from his site. What this project adds is the part that points it at *any* page: snapshotting a live DOM into a blueprint the swarm can rebuild, plus the extension around it. Go look at the original. It's better than this. ## Install **[Add it from the Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/swarm-rebuild/diaeaocnhdhbknkbfbnkjikfcgokainm)**, then pin it (puzzle icon → pin). The store version can lag behind this repo while an update is in review. To run the latest code, load it unpacked: 1. Clone or download this repo. 2. Open `chrome://extensions` and turn on **Developer mode** (top right). 3. Click **Load unpacked** and choose the [`swarm-rebuild/`](swarm-rebuild) folder. 4. Pin it (puzzle icon → pin). ## Use - Click the toolbar icon or press **Alt+Shift+S** on any page. - The page fades out and the cursors orbit the site's favicon, then fan out and start building. - **Scroll** and the swarm chases you, with more agents joining the faster you go. - **Tour** auto-scrolls at the pace the swarm can keep up with. Good for screen recordings. - **1× / 2× / 3×** changes build speed. - **Sound** is on by default (🔊 in the toolbar, or press **M**). If the page hasn't been clicked yet, Chrome keeps audio locked and the button says **Tap for sound**; one click anywhere starts it. - **Hide** hides the toolbar for clean screen recordings (or press **H**). Move your mouse to the bottom of the screen or press **H** again to show it. - When it's done, the cursors flock to your mouse. **Go live** fades back to the real, clickable page; **Replay** builds it again. - **Esc**, **✕**, or clicking the icon again exits at any time. - **Play automatically** (off by default): right-click the icon → **Options** and choose *on sites I choose* or *on every site*. Chrome asks you to allow access to those sites first, and switching back to *Only when I click* gives that access up. There's a self-contained test page in [`demo/index.html`](demo/index.html) (an inner-scrolling app shell with floats, forms, cards and media). Opening local files needs **Allow access to file URLs** enabled for the extension. ## How it works 1. **Snapshot.** [`swarm.js`](swarm-rebuild/swarm.js) walks the live DOM, including open shadow roots, and turns it into a blueprint: - boxes with fills, borders, radii, shadows, gradients, masks and backdrop blur → **rects** - text blocks → **text layers**, cloned with their computed styles (fonts, links, inline code, icons, `::before`/`::after`) - single-side borders and `
` → **pen-tool lines** - ``, `
